name: Mathematical biology
summary: Volterra and Lotka modeled predator-prey dynamics.

name: Hasse local-global principle
summary: Hasse showed a quadratic form represents zero over the rationals when it does so over all completions.

name: Commutative algebra from invariant theory and ideals
summary: Noether used chain conditions to treat primary decomposition and unique ideal factorization for abstract rings.

name: Subjective probability and decision
summary: Keynes, Ramsey and de Finetti defined probability as degree of belief, reviving Bayesian ideas against frequentism.

name: Group representations enter quantum mechanics
summary: Symmetry groups of atoms and spectra are analysed by decomposing the state space into irreducible representations, which also drives the general theory.

name: Hilbert-space quantum mechanics
to: abstract Hilbert space and unbounded operator theory
summary: Matrix and wave mechanics were unified in the Hilbert-space framework by Weyl, Dirac and von Neumann.

name: Homology groups (Noether) and algebraic topology
summary: Noether's insight that Betti numbers are ranks of groups moved topology toward group-valued invariants, and the field was renamed accordingly.

name: Rigorous foundations of algebraic geometry via commutative algebra
summary: Van der Waerden, Zariski and Weil used valuation and ideal theory to rebuild the Italian school's results rigorously.

name: Noncommutative algebras, representation theory and number theory
from: algebraic number theory (class field theory, p-adic local theory)
summary: Noether, Brauer and Hasse linked hypercomplex systems to commutative algebra and arithmetic via modules and cohomological ideas.

name: Mathematical general relativity: nonlinear PDE for Einstein's equations
summary: Well-posedness of the Einstein equations as a hyperbolic system is followed by global stability of Minkowski space and the analysis of shock formation.
